participant.recruitment: Caller explicitly selected one actual participant; not a representative sample.
reported_issues: English and unfamiliar terminology were the primary comprehension obstacle.
Control meanings were unclear; hover explanations were suggested.
No artifact was visible in the centre, so the judgement target was unidentified.
The right pane could not be scrolled and its content overlapped the lower pane.
The top pane occupied too much space.
participant.treatment: Recorded as observations and not rewritten after the repair; no post-repair participant result exists.

repair.scope: Presentation only: ui-model display text/labels, desktop-gpui shell/inspector/intervention/palette/stop/dock/flow, app-core surface labels, plus the help module. No new dependency, public protocol type, unsafe/FFI, Runtime semantic, media implementation or persistence change.
changes: User-facing headings, axis labels, button names, surface names, notices and unavailable reasons use Japanese; closed protocol statuses carry a Japanese gloss plus the canonical token, while Runtime identities, free text, artifact/evidence summaries and unknown values stay verbatim.
Every explained control keeps its accessible name/description and gains a lazy hover explanation rendered only when hovered (help module).

The inspector is its own scroll container with hidden overflow, so expanded sections stay reachable and never overlap the Candidate Dock; the work surface contains its text instead of overflowing horizontally.
The header keeps the same six state axes but no longer repeats multi-line explanations, reducing its height; the Stop row states its own condition inline.
The Artifact surface states that the current version cannot display artifact images and that only candidate explanation text is shown; no placeholder image or simulated success is used.
Dock iteration gutters show the full 反復 N label and the group-start marker moved to the candidate label, so the iteration axis stays legible in a narrow card.
Withheld/unavailable publications discard the per-consumer derivation cache again, keeping the documented invalidation invariant.
Removed source-text tests only; the weakened evidence/refinement/dock assertions were restored as field-level and reason-level checks.

findings: A-R1-01: the Accepted stop receipt no longer showed the acceptance-versus-completion distinction in the normal display because stop-detail had been gated behind manual intervention; the detail is rendered unconditionally again and the Accepted caveat is asserted in the model test.
A-R1-02: the inspector printed formal_status and evidence status tokens without a Japanese gloss; both now use a gloss plus canonical token, and unknown values stay verbatim.

review_rounds.result: both round-1 findings are closed; the reviewer confirmed that no further fix is required and that participant comprehension, the five-second condition and product acceptance stay incomplete

findings: A-R1-01: the compare hint claimed both side-change controls were unavailable whenever one side was missing, but a pending A side keeps its own change available; the hint is now keyed to the same booleans as the click gating and unit-tested across the three states.

A-R1-02: the reconnect detail promised a re-fetch although a window without a runtime endpoint has no handle and only reports that nothing can be reconnected; the detail now states that the re-fetch happens only when a connection target exists.

review_rounds.result: both round-3 findings are closed and no new finding was raised; the reviewer accepted that the pending-A state is guaranteed by source and unit test only, and kept MP-UX1 comprehension, product acceptance, MP-TYP1 and MP-R0B unchanged

review_rounds.verdict: BLOCKING 2 / ACTIONABLE NON-BLOCKING 2 / EXCESSIVE 0 (unparsed footer, read manually)
findings: B-R1-01: search matches were drawn first, so within-layer order could differ from authoritative order; matching now only decides inclusion under the cap and the drawn set is restored to authoritative order, with a test.

B-R1-02: the drawing carried neither the projected connection kind nor an explicit direction; each edge now shows its projected kind and an arrow at the projected target, and the kind is carried in DiagramEdge with a test.
A-R1-01: emphasis ignored the GraphRevision boundary; match sets are now keyed by (GraphRef, identity) with a cross-revision test, matching the list-key boundary.

A-R1-02: truncation happened before layering, so a drawn node could lose its depth and a cycle through an omitted node went unreported; depth and cycle detection now run over the complete graph before the bounded selection.

review_rounds.verdict: BLOCKING 1 / ACTIONABLE NON-BLOCKING 1 / EXCESSIVE 0 (unparsed footer, read manually)
findings: B-R2-01: whole-graph layering was O(V*(V+E)) and ran synchronously from render; layers() now condenses strongly connected components iteratively and takes the longest path over the condensation in O(V+E), the result is cached per admitted revision and only computed while the Flow surface is shown, and 10k-chain, two-node-cycle and self-loop tests pin the behavior.

A-R2-01: an upward (cyclic) edge produced negative-height segments that were clamped, so the connector did not reach its target and the arrow always pointed down; connectors are now normalized rectangles with an upward/downward marker, covered by direction tests.

review_rounds.verdict: BLOCKING 0 / ACTIONABLE NON-BLOCKING 2 / EXCESSIVE 0 (unparsed footer, read manually)
findings: A-R3-01: cards on one layer share a depth, so a same-layer cycle edge crossed the card boxes and its arrow was hidden; same-layer and self-loop edges now route above the cards with a visible target marker, covered by geometry tests.

A-R3-02: the O(V+E) claim did not match the ordered-map/set implementation; the node index and condensation deduplication now use expected-constant hash lookup and a per-target stamp, so the pass is O(V+E), and the comment states that.

review_rounds.verdict: BLOCKING 0 / ACTIONABLE NON-BLOCKING 2 / EXCESSIVE 0 (unparsed footer, read manually)
findings: A-R4-01: a depth-0 same-layer route used negative canvas coordinates; drawings with same-layer or self-loop connectors now reserve a 26 px top margin and the tests assert the route, marker and label offset stay inside the canvas.
A-R4-02: the self-loop channel sat inside the card; the connector now takes the card half-width and routes the loop outside the card, with a test on the channel position.

review_rounds.verdict: BLOCKING 0 / ACTIONABLE NON-BLOCKING 1 / EXCESSIVE 0 (unparsed footer, read manually)
findings: A-R5-01: the self-loop arrow sat on the outside channel instead of marking the same card; the loop now returns over the card just above its top edge and the marker points down at that edge, with tests for the return leg and marker position.

owner_approved_changes.approval: Caller, 2026-10-31: show Flow as a diagram; the other three items are approved in the proposed state
changes: Flow renders the authoritative graph as a layered diagram: depth is the longest path over projected edges, lanes keep authoritative order, labels/layers/identities are copied from the projection, matching search filters highlight and dim nodes, and cycles, endpoints missing from the drawing and the node cap are stated rather than hidden. The intervention row states 次にすること with the row's action and keeps the effect sentence (a re-fetch only when a connection target exists; no task start or stop).

stack_defect.fix: the diagram region is built by a dedicated flow_diagram_region function, keeping render small; the shipped binary reports SizeOfStackReserve 1048576 and starts normally
